blocks.text: A surgeon removes an enlarged lymph node from the side of a patient's neck, just behind the sternocleidomastoid. Weeks later the patient's shoulder droops, the shoulder blade sticks out when the arm is raised, and she cannot shrug. A superficial nerve that crosses a triangle of the neck, in the path of the scalpel, was injured.

blocks.markdown:
**Innervation of the face.** Two cranial nerves share the work: the **trigeminal** (V) provides **sensation** and the **facial** (VII) provides **motor** control of expression.

**Sensory (trigeminal).** The three divisions supply distinct strips of skin: **ophthalmic (V1)** the forehead, upper eyelid and the dorsum of the nose (including the cornea); **maxillary (V2)** the lower eyelid, cheek and upper lip (the terminal branch is the **infraorbital nerve**); **mandibular (V3)** the lower lip, chin, jaw and part of the ear and temple. The angle of the mandible is supplied by the great auricular nerve (C2-C3), not the trigeminal.

**Motor.** The **facial nerve** leaves the skull through the stylomastoid foramen, enters the **parotid gland** (it does not supply it) and divides into five terminal branches: **temporal, zygomatic, buccal, marginal mandibular and cervical** (supplying the muscles of expression and platysma). The **mandibular division (V3)** supplies the **muscles of mastication** (masseter, temporalis, medial and lateral pterygoids).

rows: Forehead, upper eyelid, dorsum of nose, cornea
Lower eyelid, cheek, upper lip, side of nose
Lower lip, chin, lower jaw, anterior two thirds of the ear and temple

blocks.title: Which facial branch was injured?
blocks.prompt: After surgery on the submandibular region, a patient's lower lip droops on one side when smiling, but the forehead and eye closure are normal. Which nerve branch is most likely injured and why?

steps.text: The muscles of facial expression are supplied by branches of the facial nerve. Lower-lip depressors are supplied by the marginal mandibular branch.
The marginal mandibular branch runs along the lower border of the mandible and into the neck, so it is vulnerable in submandibular surgery.
The temporal and zygomatic branches supply the forehead and eye closure, which are normal.

blocks.answer: The marginal mandibular branch of the facial nerve.

blocks.markdown: **The orbit and extraocular muscles.** Six muscles move each eye, plus the levator palpebrae superioris, which raises the upper lid. The four recti arise from a common tendinous ring at the back of the orbit; the superior oblique passes through a pulley (the trochlea). Nerve supply follows the shorthand **LR6 SO4 AO3**: the lateral rectus by the **abducens (VI)**, the superior oblique by the **trochlear (IV)**, and all the rest, including the levator palpebrae, by the **oculomotor (III)**.

blocks.title: Which muscle elevates the eye in each position?
blocks.prompt: Explain why the examiner tests the superior rectus with the eye abducted and the inferior oblique with the eye adducted.

steps.text: The superior rectus runs along the line of the orbit, which points slightly outward. When the eye is abducted its line of pull aligns with the visual axis, so its main action is pure elevation.
The inferior oblique pulls from the front and medial side of the orbit. When the eye is adducted its line of pull aligns with the visual axis and it becomes the main elevator.
Asking the patient to look up and out tests the superior rectus (III); looking up and in tests the inferior oblique (III).

blocks.answer: Muscles act best as primary movers when the gaze direction aligns with their line of pull: superior rectus in abduction, inferior oblique in adduction. The same logic gives the inferior rectus (down and out) and superior oblique (down and in).

blocks.markdown:
**The triangles of the neck.** The **sternocleidomastoid (SCM)** divides each side of the neck into an **anterior triangle** and a **posterior triangle**.

**Anterior triangle**: bounded by the anterior border of the SCM, the midline and the lower border of the mandible. It is subdivided by the digastric and omohyoid muscles into the **submental, submandibular, carotid and muscular** triangles. Contents include the **carotid sheath** (common carotid artery, internal jugular vein and vagus nerve), the **thyroid gland**, larynx and trachea, the hyoid bone and infrahyoid muscles, the hypoglossal nerve and the submandibular gland.

**Posterior triangle**: bounded by the posterior border of the SCM, the anterior border of the trapezius and the middle third of the clavicle. Contents include the **accessory nerve (XI)** running superficially, the **roots and trunks of the brachial plexus**, the **external jugular vein**, the third part of the **subclavian artery**, and cervical and supraclavicular lymph nodes. The accessory nerve crosses the triangle superficially and is vulnerable to surgical injury.

rows: Midline, anterior border of SCM, lower border of mandible
Carotid sheath, thyroid, larynx, trachea, hypoglossal nerve, submandibular gland, infrahyoid muscles
Posterior border of SCM, anterior border of trapezius, middle third of clavicle
Accessory nerve, brachial plexus roots and trunks, external jugular vein, subclavian artery (third part), supraclavicular nodes

blocks.title: Check by function
blocks.text: The SCM is supplied by the accessory nerve and divides the neck into two triangles. The anterior triangle holds midline visceral structures and the carotid sheath; the posterior triangle holds the nerves to the shoulder and arm.

blocks.title: Sensory versus motor for the face
blocks.text: Weakness of facial expression means the facial nerve (VII); loss of facial sensation or weakness of chewing means the trigeminal nerve (V). Do not mix them: a patient can have loss of facial sensation with normal facial expression.

points: Facial sensation is trigeminal (V1, V2, V3); facial expression is facial nerve (five terminal branches); mastication is V3.
The extraocular muscles follow LR6 SO4 AO3, and each acts best as the primary mover in the gaze direction that aligns with its line of pull.
The SCM divides the neck into an anterior triangle (carotid sheath, thyroid, larynx) and a posterior triangle (accessory nerve, brachial plexus roots and trunks, external jugular vein).

questions.stem: A 50-year-old man has numbness of the skin of the cheek, the lower eyelid and the upper lip after a fracture of the orbital floor. Which nerve is most likely affected?

options.text: Marginal mandibular branch of the facial nerve

distractorRationale.a: Correct: the infraorbital nerve supplies the cheek, lower eyelid and upper lip and runs in the orbital floor.
distractorRationale.b: The supraorbital nerve supplies the forehead and upper eyelid.
distractorRationale.c: The mental nerve supplies the lower lip and chin.
distractorRationale.d: A motor branch would not cause numbness.

questions.explanation: The infraorbital nerve is the terminal sensory branch of V2 and runs along the floor of the orbit, so orbital floor fractures commonly cause numbness of its territory.

questions.stem: Which nerve supplies the muscles of mastication?

options.text: Maxillary division of the trigeminal nerve
Mandibular division of the trigeminal nerve

questions.correctOptionText: Mandibular division of the trigeminal nerve

distractorRationale.a: The facial nerve supplies muscles of expression.
distractorRationale.c: Correct: V3 carries motor fibres to masseter, temporalis and the pterygoids.
distractorRationale.d: The hypoglossal nerve supplies the tongue.

questions.explanation: The mandibular division is the only trigeminal division with a motor component. It supplies the muscles of mastication.

questions.stem: After a laceration across the temple, a patient cannot raise the right eyebrow or wrinkle the right forehead. Which branch of the facial nerve is most likely divided?

distractorRationale.b: The buccal branch supplies the cheek and upper lip.
distractorRationale.c: The marginal mandibular branch supplies the lower lip.
distractorRationale.d: Correct: the temporal branch supplies frontalis and the upper orbicularis oculi.

questions.explanation: The temporal branch crosses the zygomatic arch and supplies frontalis, which raises the eyebrow and wrinkles the forehead. It is the branch most exposed to temple lacerations.

questions.stem: Which extraocular muscle is supplied by the abducens nerve?

distractorRationale.a: The medial rectus is supplied by CN III.
distractorRationale.c: The superior oblique is supplied by CN IV.
distractorRationale.d: The inferior rectus is supplied by CN III.

questions.explanation: The abducens nerve (CN VI) supplies the lateral rectus, which abducts the eye.

questions.stem: A 28-year-old man has double vision when he looks down and toward his nose in his left eye, for example when going downstairs. Which muscle and nerve are most likely affected?

options.text: Left superior oblique and the trochlear nerve
Left inferior rectus and the oculomotor nerve
Left lateral rectus and the abducens nerve
Left inferior oblique and the oculomotor nerve

questions.correctOptionText: Left superior oblique and the trochlear nerve

distractorRationale.a: Correct: the superior oblique is the main depressor when the eye is adducted, and CN IV supplies it.
distractorRationale.b: The inferior rectus is the main depressor when the eye is abducted.
distractorRationale.c: The lateral rectus abducts the eye.
distractorRationale.d: The inferior oblique elevates the eye.

questions.explanation: Looking down and in (adducted) depends on the superior oblique, which is supplied by the trochlear nerve. Weakness produces double vision that is worst on this movement, as when reading or walking downstairs.

questions.stem: True or false: the inferior oblique muscle is supplied by the trochlear nerve.
questions.explanation: The inferior oblique is supplied by the oculomotor nerve (CN III). The trochlear nerve supplies only the superior oblique, as the LR6 SO4 AO3 rule states.

questions.stem: Which structure lies in the posterior triangle of the neck?

options.text: Common carotid artery within the carotid sheath

distractorRationale.a: The carotid sheath lies in the anterior triangle.
distractorRationale.b: The thyroid gland lies in the anterior triangle.
distractorRationale.c: Correct: roots and trunks of the brachial plexus pass through the posterior triangle.
distractorRationale.d: The hyoid bone lies in the anterior part of the neck.

questions.explanation: The brachial plexus roots and trunks emerge between the scalene muscles and cross the lower part of the posterior triangle. The thyroid, carotid sheath and hyoid belong to the anterior triangle and midline.

questions.stem: Which three structures lie within the carotid sheath in the anterior triangle?

options.text: Common carotid artery, internal jugular vein and vagus nerve
Common carotid artery, external jugular vein and accessory nerve
Subclavian artery, internal jugular vein and phrenic nerve
Internal carotid artery, thyroid gland and hypoglossal nerve

questions.correctOptionText: Common carotid artery, internal jugular vein and vagus nerve

distractorRationale.b: The external jugular vein and accessory nerve are in the posterior triangle.
distractorRationale.c: The subclavian artery and phrenic nerve are not in the carotid sheath.
distractorRationale.d: The thyroid gland is not in the sheath.

questions.explanation: The carotid sheath contains the common (and then internal) carotid artery, the internal jugular vein and the vagus nerve. It lies deep to the anterior border of the SCM.

questions.stem: Which of the following correctly lists the boundaries of the anterior triangle of the neck?

options.text: Posterior border of SCM, anterior border of trapezius and middle third of the clavicle
Anterior border of SCM, midline and lower border of the mandible
Midline, clavicle and lower border of the mandible
Anterior border of SCM, anterior border of trapezius and hyoid bone

questions.correctOptionText: Anterior border of SCM, midline and lower border of the mandible

distractorRationale.c: The clavicle is not a boundary of the anterior triangle.
distractorRationale.d: The trapezius bounds the posterior triangle.

questions.explanation: The anterior triangle is bounded by the anterior border of the sternocleidomastoid, the midline of the neck and the lower border of the mandible, forming an inverted triangle with its apex at the sternal notch.

questions.stem: A patient has a mass in the posterior triangle of the neck. Describe the boundaries of this triangle and list the main structures that would be at risk during surgery in this area, with the consequence of damage to one of them.
markingGuide: Boundaries: posterior border of sternocleidomastoid, anterior border of trapezius, middle third of clavicle
Contents: accessory nerve (superficial), roots and trunks of the brachial plexus, external jugular vein, third part of subclavian artery, supraclavicular lymph nodes
Accessory nerve injury causes weakness of trapezius and sternocleidomastoid, shoulder droop and inability to shrug
Brachial plexus damage causes weakness or sensory loss in the upper limb
questions.explanation: The posterior triangle contains structures serving the shoulder and arm in addition to vessels and nodes. The accessory nerve is superficial and therefore most vulnerable, and its injury drops the shoulder.
